svg.title: Command
svg.desc: Command. Turn a request into an object that can be queued, logged, undone and redone, decoupling who asks from who acts. Step 1, Buttons call methods: The toolbar calls the Document directly. Nothing records the edits, so Ctrl+Z has nothing to undo. Step 2, Requests as objects: Each edit becomes a command object. History runs it and pushes it: Hello → Hello world → world. Step 3, Undo and redo: Undo pops a command and calls its undo(): world → Hello world → Hello. Redo runs it again. Step 4, Queue, log, replay: A command is an object, so it can wait in a queue, go into a log to be replayed, or join a macro.

g.text: The toolbar calls the Document directly. Nothing records the edits, so Ctrl+Z has nothing to undo.
Each edit becomes a command object. History runs it and pushes it: Hello → Hello world → world.
Undo pops a command and calls its undo(): world → Hello world → Hello. Redo runs it again.
A command is an object, so it can wait in a queue, go into a log to be replayed, or join a macro.

A command holds its receiver (doc), its arguments (at, s, n) and what its undo() needs (removed)
Redo rule executing a new command clears the redo stack: the undone edits no longer fit the text
